quickfire.question: A doubly linked list node has two pointers. What do they point to?

routineWriter.questionText: Write the node declaration for a doubly linked list in C.

commonMistakes.description: The prev pointer is what distinguishes doubly from singly — must not be forgotten
Both pointers must be typed struct DNode*, not int or void*

quickfire.question: When inserting a new node N after target T in a doubly linked list, N->prev must be set to _____.

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for insertAfter in a doubly linked list. The function receives a pointer to the target node and the value to insert after it.

commonMistakes.description: New node's prev must point back to the target — this is the extra link that makes it doubly
Guard before updating successor's prev — target may be the last node
Successor's prev must be updated to point to the new node, not the old predecessor
This line must come LAST — updating it before saves n->next correctly

quickfire.question: Deleting a middle node from a doubly linked list requires updating how many pointers (not counting the deleted node itself)?

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine to delete a given node from a doubly linked list. The node to delete is passed directly (not searched by value).

commonMistakes.description: If target is the head (prev is NULL), head pointer itself must be updated
Successor's prev must skip over the deleted node
Must free after relinking — freeing first corrupts the pointer reads
